value.title: Seat capabilities: secured issuer, socket and send-as gate (PRD 003 req-10, plan 221 phase 2)
value.summary: Each seat incarnation gets a private capability from a secured issuer, every client presents it (counted, not yet enforced), and send-as is the first operation that refuses callers without it.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Plan 221 decided the design (workshop 001, option C). This plan builds it in two PRs. Phase A: the secured issuer (nonce, token, transactions, revocation), the Unix socket with peer credentials and the fresh boundary walk, one owned session per incarnation, every client presenting the capability, and per-operation counters; nothing is refused except issuance. Phase B, after phase A is deployed and the evidence window holds: send-as refuses callers without the capability, closing #152's residual. The other classes (inbox-claim, controls, role-and-holder, outputs, registration, activity, attribution) follow in a later plan by the same evidence rule. One coder.

sections.name: goals
value: Each seat incarnation gets a private capability from a secured issuer, every client presents it (counted, not yet enforced), and send-as is the first operation that refuses callers without it.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Enforcing any class after send-as (inbox-claim, controls, role-and-holder, outputs, registration, activity, attribution): a later plan, one class at a time by the same evidence rule.
PRD 003 permission policy (req-01 to req-09) and q-02 to q-04, which are the prime's; sidecar, system-message and exemption rules are not decided here.
Defending against a same-user attacker reading another process's memory or environment, or typing into its pane (the workshop's stated limit).
Keeping /new working in a pij Copilot seat (ruled out by the one-owned-session ruling).

value.claim: Inventory metadata is correct before anything consumes it. Squirrel's three LOW notes on #163 (governance 7e537dc) are fixed in harness/scripts/route-inventory.json: the registration entry describes the ordinary (non-native) branch's guard, not only native N; POST background's authority names parent; the compact-self send aliases name their parent-authorized controls. Every seat-authority entry names the operation class the gate uses (send-as, inbox-claim, controls, role-and-holder, outputs, registration, activity, attribution), and shared handlers that reach a write through another URI list each operation they reach (workshop contract e). Implicit HEAD keeps its GET's class.

The issuer is secured first (workshop contracts a and b). Spawn and revive mint a single-use nonce (32 bytes from the OS random source), store only its digest with spawn id, intended seat, harness, issue time and expiry, and pass the nonce to the harness through the spawn environment. Registration presenting it does, in ONE store transaction: find an unconsumed, unexpired nonce matching spawn and intended seat; mark it consumed; create or bind the incarnation; store the new token's digest (32 independent random bytes). Any failure commits nothing; the loser of a race is refused E-RS-SPAWN-NONCE-USED and an anomaly is recorded. A registration carrying only public facts (TCP or socket, no nonce, no peer-credential boundary) still registers as today but gets NO token and NO context grant (closes F88 row 2); the context grant is issued only through this issuer and is folded into the capability. Rotation is two-phase (the old digest stays valid until the new token is first presented). Tombstone, supersede and observed-dead owner delete the incarnation's digests in the transaction that records the change. Nonce and token digests persist across a daemon bounce (one migration: main's highest + 1 at push time). Expired nonces are dropped when their spawn is next touched or at daemon start; no sweep.

Peer credentials on a Unix socket, and the boundary walk (workshop contract c). The daemon adds `<state-dir>/daemon.sock` (0600, in a 0700 directory) serving the same router as TCP. Credentials come only from `UnixStream::peer_cred()` on the accepted stream, read once at accept; a missing pid, an error, or a uid other than the daemon's refuses every seat-authority request on that connection, never falling back to body identifiers. The peer's start is read in-process at accept and re-read on every request. A tokenless request walks from the peer pid to the NEAREST registered harness boundary (pid plus start), at most 16 hops, every hop read fresh, in-process only (`parent_and_name` and `observed_start`; on Linux the parent from /proc/<pid>/stat field 4); never the ProcLiveness wrapper, never `ps`. Reaching pid 1, launchd or a tmux server, using up 16 hops, or an unreadable hop is refused E-RS-SEAT-PROVENANCE. No ancestry cache. The only index is boundary (pid, start) to live incarnations, maintained by registration events in the same transactions, capped at 4,096 entries (a new registration at the cap is refused E-RS-SEAT-INDEX-FULL; nothing is evicted). Adopted and hand-started seats bootstrap their token through this path at registration over the socket.

One owned session per incarnation (workshop session ownership, ruled by the prime 08 Nov). The owner is the process that bootstrapped the incarnation (Copilot: that session's extension host; OMP, Pi, Claude, Codex: the harness process) and holds the token in memory. Ownership moves only by presenting the current token or after the owner is observed dead. A boundary owning two or more live sessions refuses tokenless authority with exactly: `E-RS-SEAT-AMBIGUOUS: this Copilot process hosts more than one live session; start a fresh seat (pij-rs revive --fresh), don't /new` (the harness name adjusted for non-Copilot). Public session ids and precedence observations never decide ownership; the extension hosts' own token-bearing requests are unaffected.

Secrets stay where the workshop puts them (contract d). Tokens live only in the owning process's memory and the registration response to it: never in a subprocess environment or argv, and never in diagnostics, logs, /health, the roster, cards or the spine. The nonce is the only secret in an environment, single-use and peer-checked at use (a nonce registration must arrive over the socket from a process whose nearest boundary is the spawned pane's process). The optional remote listener never accepts a capability-bearing request; paired machines keep their three-route scope. A socket or probe failure never falls back to key-plus-identifiers authority: it is counted as neither, and refused once its class is enforced.

Every client presents the capability (phase 2a rollout). The native Copilot extension, the OMP and Pi extensions keep the token in memory from their registration response and send it on every seat-authority request over the socket (loopback TCP with the token where the socket is unavailable). The `pij` shim, `pij-rs`, and the Claude, Codex and Copilot hooks and status lines use the socket and act through peer credentials. Old clients keep working: nothing is refused in this phase except issuance. Before relying on hooks, the coder confirms Claude hooks run below the Claude process in every pij launch mode; if not, stop and tell pm-001 (the workshop's open question).

Counting by operation (phase 2a). The daemon counts every seat-authority operation, by class and outcome (token, peer-credential, neither) plus nonce-authenticated first registrations, as bounded counters in /health (class x outcome, no per-seat or per-request rows). Counting follows the operation, wherever it is reached (shared handlers, aliases, implicit HEAD), not the URI.

Send-as is enforced, first (phase 2b, the prime's requirement; closes #152's pane-replay residual). After phase A is merged and deployed, every send-as operation (`/v1/send`, `/v1/shim/send`, and every alias or shared handler that sends, such as the compact-self send aliases) refuses a caller without the capability (no token, no peer-credential boundary) with E-RS-SEAT-CAPABILITY, whose text tells an old client what to update. The caller is not the target: a parent, PA or prime acting on another seat passes the existing checks as itself. The flip ships only on positive evidence: every representative client completed a capability-proven send on the live fleet, a negative test shows the same send without the capability refused, and the send-as 'neither' counter delta was zero over a working day on traffic-bearing send routes. `a_client_replaying_a_live_seats_pane_still_replies_as_it_until_req_10` (crates/daemon/tests/directory_http.rs) flips to a refusal and is renamed, never deleted.

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). Per the workshop's cost table. A long-lived token request adds one SHA-256 of 32 bytes, a constant-time compare and a lookup in a warm digest map. A tokenless request adds one peer-credential read per connection, a start re-read per request, and a walk of at most 16 hops (typically 1 to 3), each an in-process parent read, a start read and one hash lookup in the boundary index; no roster scan, no census. Nothing launches per request, so nothing per tick per seat. Bootstrap and rotation run once per incarnation (any C27 `ps` argv check stays here). Lifecycle: one store read of live digests after a bounce; nonces expire with the registration window, no sweep; the boundary index is capped at 4,096 and event-maintained. Measure before and after deploy: ping .data.spawns per call site and just spawn-rate, plus daemon CPU at rest with the fleet live, since every per-tick heartbeat, inbox and activity call now carries the check.

Docs and states. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md: the Seat authority section gains the socket, the token and nonce, the refusals E-RS-SPAWN-NONCE-USED, E-RS-SEAT-PROVENANCE, E-RS-SEAT-INDEX-FULL, E-RS-SEAT-AMBIGUOUS and E-RS-SEAT-CAPABILITY, and the per-class enforcement state; docs/difficulties.md: F88 send-as closed, the other classes open; workstream 003 s01 stays in-progress (classes after send-as are a follow-up plan); the skill says not to /new in a pij Copilot seat (revive --fresh instead). docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

value.title: Phase A: secured issuer, socket, ownership, clients and counting (count-only)
value.brief: Two PRs, both count-only (nothing refused except issuance). A1, the daemon: AC1 to AC5 and AC7, plus cost and docs. A2, the clients: AC6 (the Copilot, OMP and Pi extensions present the token; the shim, pij-rs and hooks use the socket), plus cost and docs. A2 merges before phase B's evidence window starts.

value.title: Phase B: enforce send-as
value.brief: AC8, plus cost and docs. A second PR, opened only after phase A is deployed and the evidence window (every client proven, a working day of zero 'neither' on traffic-bearing send routes) holds.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Plan 221 phase 1 (#163, merged ed9a3d7c) shipped the route inventory sensor (77 pairs, 47 seat-authority) and workshop 001 revision 2, which recommends option C: peer credentials or a spawn nonce as bootstrap evidence, a per-incarnation hashed token as the per-request control, boundary-limited ancestry for short-lived clients, one owned session per incarnation (ruled by the prime 08 Nov), issuer first, then gate operations send-as first. Verdicts on 95bbd70: spoonbill (governance 889d432), squirrel (7e537dc, three LOW inventory notes, fixed here in AC1), ocelot (6ac90d5). C32 accepts F88-class residuals until req-10; #152's Known limit (send-as through any raw 'from' and pane replay) closes in AC8. PRD 003 q-02 to q-04 (permission policy) are open and prime-owned; nothing here depends on them. If a choice turns out to, stop and ask pm-001.

value.question: Do Claude hooks run below the Claude process in every pij launch mode? If not, Claude needs a long-lived owner to hold the token. The coder confirms in phase A before relying on hooks, and stops and tells pm-001 if not.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
